title: Pacific Coast Highway: San Francisco to Los Angeles
summary: A 3-day drive down California's Highway 1, hugging the coast from San Francisco to Los Angeles. Expect stunning cliff views, fresh seafood, and at least one stop that makes you consider moving there.

stops.goal: Start the trip with a photo at the iconic northern overlook before heading south
stops.notes: Parking fills fast on weekends. Arrive before 9am or expect a wait.

stops.goal: Grab an early lunch with ocean views before the coast road narrows

alternatives.goal: The one Taco Bell with a Pacific Ocean view — genuinely worth it
alternatives.notes: Yes, really. It's a meme, but the view is real.

stops.goal: Walk the beach and decompress — first proper coastal stop of the trip
stops.notes: Water is cold year-round. Bring a layer — it's windier than it looks.

stops.goal: Stretch, grab a snack, and catch the sunset over the boardwalk
stops.notes: The Giant Dipper roller coaster is a legit historic landmark (1924). Free to walk the boardwalk.

stops.goal: Overnight stay — good base for Day 2's Big Sur drive
stops.notes: Book ahead in summer. The Cannery Row area puts you close to the aquarium and Fisherman's Wharf.

alternatives.goal: Quieter, more upscale overnight option 10 min south of Monterey
alternatives.notes: Charming but pricier. Good choice if you want to avoid the Cannery Row tourist density.

stops.goal: Morning scenic drive through Pebble Beach — Lone Cypress is the money shot
stops.notes: Entrance fee (~$12/vehicle as of 2024). Worth it. Opens at sunrise.

stops.goal: The iconic Big Sur viewpoint — pull over here, full stop
stops.notes: Tiny pullout on the north side of the bridge fills instantly. If full, loop back — it turns over fast. Check for road closures on Caltrans before this leg; Highway 1 through Big Sur has a history of washouts.

stops.goal: Purple-sand beach with a rock arch — one of the weirdest and best beaches in California
stops.notes: Easy to miss — look for Sycamore Canyon Rd, unmarked. Cash or app payment at the gate. The purple sand is real (manganese garnet).

stops.goal: Overnight stay — positioned for an early Hearst Castle visit on Day 3
stops.notes: San Simeon is tiny; Cambria (5 min south) has more restaurant options. Elephant seals at Piedras Blancas rookery just north — check at dusk or dawn.

alternatives.goal: Larger town with more dining, 30 min south — good if Cambria feels too remote

location.name: Hearst Castle
location.address: 750 Hearst Castle Rd, San Simeon, CA 93452

stops.goal: Tour the most absurd private home in American history
stops.notes: Tickets must be booked in advance online. Multiple tour types — Grand Rooms is the best first-timer option.

stops.goal: Lunch stop in a genuinely great college town — Bubble Gum Alley is optional but mandatory

alternatives.goal: Skip SLO and eat clam chowder on the pier instead
alternatives.notes: The clam chowder in a sourdough bowl is not a cliché — it's just correct.

location.name: Santa Monica Pier, Los Angeles
location.address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401

stops.goal: End of Route 66 marker — touch the sign, get a photo, call it done
stops.notes: You made it. The pier itself is touristy but the symbolism is real. Sunset here is a solid finish to the drive.
